issues.description: Card number validation only checks length (16 characters) without performing Luhn algorithm validation. This allows invalid card numbers to pass validation.
issues.suggestion: Implement Luhn algorithm validation for credit card numbers to ensure they are mathematically valid before processing payment.

issues.description: Payment card details (cardNumber, expiryDate, cvv) are stored in plain text in memory and database. Card data should never be stored; only tokenized references should be kept.
issues.suggestion: Use a PCI-compliant payment gateway that handles tokenization. Never store raw card details. Store only the last 4 digits and a payment token.

issues.description: Payment processing stores card data in the database (line 113: lastFour is derived from full cardNumber). Even storing last 4 digits without proper encryption violates PCI-DSS compliance.
issues.suggestion: Use a third-party payment processor (Stripe, Square, etc.) that handles payment tokenization. Do not process or store card details directly.

issues.description: Expiry date parsing assumes 2-digit year format and adds 2000. This will fail for years 2100+ and creates ambiguity for dates like '99' (1999 vs 2099).
issues.suggestion: Use explicit 4-digit year format (MM/YYYY) in validation, or implement a more robust date parsing mechanism with proper error handling.

issues.description: No idempotency check for payment processing. If the function is called twice with the same parameters, it will charge the card twice.
issues.suggestion: Implement idempotency keys or check if payment already exists before processing. Store transaction IDs and verify before charging.

issues.description: JSON.parse() called without try-catch error handling. Malformed JSON in database will crash the application.
issues.suggestion: Wrap JSON.parse() in try-catch blocks with appropriate error handling and fallback values.

issues.description: JSON.parse() called without try-catch error handling on line 182. Malformed JSON in database will crash the application.
issues.suggestion: Wrap JSON.parse() in try-catch blocks with appropriate error handling and fallback values.

issues.description: No transaction management for payment + subscription upgrade. If subscription upgrade fails after payment is charged, the user will be charged without receiving the service.
issues.suggestion: Implement database transactions to ensure both payment and subscription upgrade succeed together, or provide rollback capability.

issues.description: Payment amount comparison uses < without checking for negative amounts. Negative or zero amounts could bypass validation.
issues.suggestion: Add explicit validation: amount > 0 and payment.amount >= amount with clear error messages.

issues.description: Hard-coded feature sets for tiers embedded in function. Adding new features or tiers requires code changes.
issues.suggestion: Move tier-to-features mapping to configuration file or database table for easier maintenance and feature management.

issues.description: No validation that cardNumber contains only digits. Non-numeric characters would pass the length check.
issues.suggestion: Add regex validation: /^\d{16}$/ to ensure cardNumber contains exactly 16 digits.

codeQuality.summary: This premium features module contains critical security vulnerabilities related to payment processing and PCI-DSS compliance. Most notably: (1) Raw credit card data is stored without encryption, violating industry standards; (2) Card validation lacks Luhn algorithm and digit-only checks; (3) No idempotency protection allows duplicate charges; (4) JSON parsing without error handling can crash the app; (5) No transaction management between payment and subscription upgrade creates data inconsistency risks. The code requires significant refactoring to use a PCI-compliant payment gateway and implement proper error handling and transaction management.

testCoverage.summary: File src/premium.ts is a new payment processing module with zero test coverage. It contains 6 exported/public functions and multiple helper functions handling critical business logic: payment processing, card validation, pricing calculations, subscription management, and feature access control. All functions involve multiple branching paths, financial calculations, and database operations. The code includes explicit warnings about missing tests. This is a high-risk module requiring comprehensive test coverage before production use, particularly for payment processing and security-critical card validation logic.

suggestions.description: Extract magic numbers (pricing, tax rate, processing fee) into named constants at module level for easier maintenance and configuration
suggestions.benefits: Centralizes pricing configuration, eliminates magic numbers, makes it easier to adjust pricing per tier independently

suggestions.description: Simplify date expiry validation using Date constructor more directly and avoid manual year offset calculation
suggestions.benefits: More explicit year calculation with radix parameter for parseInt, handles end-of-month expiry semantics correctly

suggestions.description: Extract SQL query strings and their parameter binding into a dedicated database layer module to reduce duplication and improve maintainability
suggestions.benefits: Centralizes database queries, improves testability, reduces SQL string duplication, separates concerns

suggestions.description: Extract feature list definitions into a constant mapping for easier maintenance and clarity
suggestions.benefits: Makes feature tiers explicit and easily auditable, improves readability, enables reuse across codebase

suggestions.description: Extract subscription validation logic (checking if subscription is valid) into a reusable function to avoid duplication
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates date validation duplication, centralizes subscription validity logic, improves code reusability

suggestions.description: Add optional chaining and null coalescing for safer property access and transformation
suggestions.benefits: Improves type safety and robustness against null/undefined values from database results

refactorings.summary: The premium.ts file handles critical payment and subscription logic with several opportunities for improvement. Key refactoring suggestions focus on extracting magic numbers into named constants, simplifying date validation logic, reducing code duplication in database queries, and improving type safety for payment processing. These changes will enhance maintainability, readability, and reduce the risk of bugs in payment-critical code.
